newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SOLIDARITY UNION URGES TO BLOCK SELL-OFFS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SOLIDARITY UNION URGES TO BLOCK SELL-OFFS.

text.p: Poland's Solidarity trade union, required its local representatives in state-owned firms to block privatisation unless specific demands were met, the union's national council said on Wednesday.

Marian Krzaklewski, the head of the national council, said Poland's ruling coalition, comprised of the ex-communist and peasant parties, was selling the country's top firms without giving citizens their fair shake of the revenues.
"Poland is selling shares in its best firms, which should become the base for creating retirement and pension funds. This way pension reform is seriously endangered," Krzaklewski said.

The national council said in a statement on Wednesday that Solidarity representatives working for soon-to-be-privatised state firms were obliged to block all sell-off measures unless the government fulfils the following requirements:

Packets of shares of privatised firms had to be guaranteed for its employes, for a programme of a nationwide distribution of state assets to all citizens, for reprivatisation claims, and for pension and retirement funds.
Also the state treasury had to keep an "appropriate controling stake" of firms in strategic economic and financial sectors as well as guarantee a social benefit package for workers.
Solidarity's national council warned that if the ruling coaltition's privatisation course was not changed soon it would stage protests on a wide scale.

Krzaklewski said the union's priority would be to investigate this year's sale of Bank Slaski SA to Dutch ING Groep NV in which the Dutch bank upped its share to a majority stake in one of the country's leading commercial banks.
"It (Slaski's privatisation) was a crime against the state," Krzaklewski said.
